title: Priyanka Chopra Just Dropped the Jolie Bombshell — and Her 2027 Slate Is Obscene
excerpt: From a mystery project with Angelina Jolie to Rajamouli's ₹1,400-crore Varanasi, Mira Nair's Amri, and a comedy with Will Ferrell — Priyanka isn't just back, she's everywhere
body:
There's busy, there's booked, and then there's **Priyanka Chopra Jonas** casually confirming she's working with **Angelina Jolie** and refusing to tell anyone what it is.

In a wide-ranging interview with *Fortune India* published this week, Chopra dropped the kind of line that sends entertainment desks scrambling. "I will be working with Angelina Jolie on a project," she said — and then, with the serenity of someone who has five films in various stages of production, declined to elaborate. Film? Campaign? Humanitarian venture? "You'll see."

What we do know is the company she's keeping. Chopra listed Jolie alongside **Penélope Cruz** and **Salma Hayek** as the women who inspire her most in the industry — three actresses who've built careers on their own terms, across languages and continents. That Priyanka now belongs in the same sentence isn't aspiration; it's fact.

## The Rajamouli Homecoming

The centrepiece of her comeback is, of course, **Varanasi** — and even by the standards of the man who gave us *Baahubali* and *RRR*, the scale is staggering.

Directed by **SS Rajamouli**, the globe-trotting action-adventure has been shot across **Georgia, Antarctica, Africa, and Hyderabad**, on a reported budget of **₹1,200–1,400 crore** (approximately $135–150 million), making it one of the most expensive Indian films ever produced. Chopra stars alongside **Mahesh Babu** in his Hindi debut and **Prithviraj Sukumaran**, in what Rajamouli has described as a new kind of spectacle.

> "What we are trying to do is something so ambitious and of a scale not seen for a very long time. I am very privileged and excited not just for India but also the world, because this will be a massive global release and people will be exposed to what we have been working on for the past three years." — Priyanka Chopra Jonas

Varanasi is currently scheduled for a **worldwide release on April 7, 2027**. A first glimpse screened at the **Annecy Film Festival** earlier this month drew a roaring response from a French crowd — and Rajamouli hadn't even shown them the finished product yet.

For diaspora audiences who've watched Priyanka straddle Hollywood and Bollywood for over a decade, this is the role that brings it all together — an Indian production designed to play in every market on Earth, with a desi star who already has the Hollywood Rolodex to make it land.

## The Rest of the Slate Is Ridiculous

But Varanasi is just one line on a CV that reads like someone playing career-mode on unlimited resources.

There's **Reset**, a PPP co-production opposite **Orlando Bloom**. There's **Amri**, a biographical drama directed by the great **Mira Nair** — the woman behind *Monsoon Wedding* and *The Namesake*, two films that defined diaspora cinema for a generation. And there's **Judgment Day**, a Nicholas Stoller comedy featuring **Will Ferrell**, **Zac Efron**, and **Regina Hall** — the kind of ensemble Hollywood comedy where you show up, have fun, and let two hundred million people see your face.

Priyanka herself seems aware of the shift. Quoting her husband **Nick Jonas**, who paraphrased **Beyoncé**, she told *Fortune India*: "You are on the other side of your sacrifice." After years of building credibility in a system that wasn't built for her, she can now choose — and she's choosing everything.

## What the Diaspora Should Know

For NRI audiences, the practical upside is enormous. **Varanasi** will be released theatrically worldwide — expect IMAX and premium format bookings in every major diaspora city. The Jolie collaboration is likely to generate global English-language press that puts Indian storytelling front and centre. **Amri** with Mira Nair is almost certainly a streaming play that'll land on a platform accessible everywhere. And **Judgment Day** is a studio comedy that'll be in every AMC and Odeon from opening weekend.

Priyanka has never had a year where this many projects converge at this level. She's not straddling two industries anymore — she's running them simultaneously, with the kind of creative leverage that comes from being the only person in the room who can open a film in Mumbai and Manhattan.

"I love the film and TV medium and have not kept a glass ceiling for myself," she said. "I lead with my curiosity."

Curiosity. Sure. What she has is a monopoly.
